The consolidation contract allocates 8007 to this lab. CONSOLIDATION CONFLICT, recorded rather than rediscovered: 8007 is ALSO lab 6's internal port (its real MCP server, behind the proxy on 8006). models.shared_note: SHARED with labs 3, 4, 5 and 6. Bought by lab 3. Lab 7 buys NO model and no new package of any kind - the THIRD lab running to add zero new bytes.

measured.reencoding_works: json, csv, kv, xml, urlq, yaml - 6/6 field values kept, byte-identical across 3 runs at temperature 0. Five of these ship; yaml is held in reserve.
measured.ini_fails: 0/6 fields. Returns the key names as bare [section] headers and DROPS every value - confidently, and identically on three runs. Refused by variants.py with the measurement attached; expert mode invites the student to try it.
measured.syslog_fails: 6/6 fields but no RFC 3164 framing at all - it returns a comma list. Supplying a worked example made it WORSE: 5/6 fields and NOT deterministic. A worked example is not always a help on a 1.5B model.
measured.base64_fails: 0/6. Degenerate repeating loop for 48.9 s producing garbage that decodes to 'C05316716716...'. A stricter 'character by character, output only the base64' phrasing answers in 2.6 s with 'SGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=' - base64 for 'Hello world', a memorised string unrelated to the input. Hex fails the same way, decoding to 'SELINECALLEDABLE' repeating. These two were the ONLY cases in 36 generations that were not deterministic at temperature 0.
measured.why_that_matters: A model is a paraphraser, not a computer: it cannot perform an exact transform on data it has not memorised. base64 and hex are therefore produced by two lines of stdlib, labelled PYTHON on screen, and the contrast is a teaching beat. It is also why LAMEHUG (AML.CS0044) used a Qwen model for command TEXT and ordinary code for everything that had to be right.
measured.model_returns_prose: 6 of 10 cases wrapped the answer in a code fence or prefaced it with a sentence despite 'output only the encoded record, nothing else'. variants.py has an extractor; without it the detectors would be measuring our parser.

interval and jitter. Two numbers, and they are the whole of beat 6. The runner resets them to 60 / 0.0 on every run so a stale edit cannot satisfy an assertion this run never earned.

What each detector recorded. The runner asserts on this, not on screen text.

measured.note: Measured 2026-09-13, arm64, Docker 29.7.2, on the image built from lab-beta/lab7.
measured.image_on_disk: 2.64 GB - the same size as labs 5 and 6
measured.timing_note: FASTER than labs 5 and 6 at every CPU count, because lab 7 does 5 generations behind ONE model load where lab 6 did 9 behind four. The 4-cpu figure is within noise of unrestricted: generation is memory-bandwidth-bound, so past about four threads more cores buy nothing.
measured.thread_fix: FOUND AND FIXED HERE, and it affects labs 3-6 too. os.cpu_count() returns the HOST's core count (24) even inside `docker run --cpus=2`, because --cpus is a CFS quota and not a cpuset - sched_getaffinity agrees with it. llama.cpp then starts 24 threads to share 2 CPUs and thrashes. Before the fix: 541 s at --cpus=2 and 189 s at --cpus=4. After reading the cgroup v2 quota instead: 89 s and 37 s. A 6x and 5x improvement. A real student is usually unaffected, because Docker Desktop's CPU setting changes the VM's core count and os.cpu_count() sees that correctly - but anyone who caps a container is, and every documented CPU floor for labs 3-6 is pessimistic by this factor.
measured.detector_results: D1 signature 6/8 - misses base64 and hex, the two the model could not write. D2 structural 8/8. D3 behavioural FLAGGED on both limbs at 60 s / 0 % (1440 check-ins, cv 0.000, 60.00 records/h), CLEAN at 7200 s / 95 % (18 check-ins, cv 0.680, 0.75 records/h). Slowdown 80x; 500 records goes from 8 hours to 28 days.
measured.d3_negative_finding: The first D3 keyed on regularity ALONE and collapsed: 60 s with 60 % jitter is clean AND 61.04 records/h, so evasion cost 1x and the lab's ending would have been false. Two orthogonal limbs (volume > 24 per 24 h, OR cv < 0.35) restore it. Thresholds confirmed by the instructor 2026-09-13. The runner asserts on BOTH limbs, not just the verdict - sabotaging the volume limb alone left the verdict correct while the closing claim had quietly become false.
measured.determinism: byte-identical variants.json and results.json across 3 fresh containers
measured.fails_loudly: 4 deliberate sabotages tried: the D2 threshold, a format swapped for one that drops fields, the volume limb, the regularity limb. All 4 produce LAB ERROR and exit 1.
measured.typed_paths: all 8 typed -> 'You typed 8 of 8'. One step wrong twice -> command run for the student, 'You typed 7 of 8'.
measured.published_layer_sharing: PROVEN 2026-09-14 on the live registry, third lab running. lab7-arm64 shares 10 layers and 1.192 GB with lab6-arm64 - INCLUDING the 1.092 GB model layer - and a student who already has lab 6 downloads 41,538 bytes for lab 7. The 12 unshared layers are lab 7's own script COPYs and total 41 KB. Compare lab4->lab5 (different build recipes): 1,144 MB. The SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH + rewrite-timestamp + no-pycache recipe works, and it now holds across three consecutive labs.
